newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNIONS REJECT WAGE, BENEFIT CUTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNIONS REJECT WAGE, BENEFIT CUTS.

text.p: A grouping of Finnish industrial unions, Teollisuuden Palkansaajat, on Tuesday warned against further cuts in wages and jobless security and called on employers to shoulder their responsibility for employment.
"Employers do not sufficiently bear their responsibility for employment and the building of our nation's welfare," the group said in a statement.
"Companies that have made large profits are again dismissing or temporarily laying off their workers," it said.
"This short-sighted personnel policy is a serious threat to the uture of the companies," the unions said, and added that employers were creating a shortage of skilled labour.
"Recent proposals for new cuts in unemployment security and other social security will not increase employment or the well-being of citizens," Teollisuuden Palkansaajat said.
"Proposals to pay wages below the minimum wages specified in labour contracts would in fact mean the dismantling of the principle of universal coverage (of collective agreements)," it said.
"The government should not consent to this," it added.
"An idea in the right direction would be to improve the meaningfulness of work by reducing workers' taxes," it said.

Teollisuuden Palkansaajat, which brings together unions representing wage-earners in key industrial sectors such as the forest and metal industries, the chemical industry and construction, said its member unions have over 635,000 members.
